references.text: Joshua also sent spies to explore a city (Jericho), and they received help from a resident (Rahab) who showed them the way and was shown mercy in return.
Rahab asked for mercy (חֶסֶד) for herself and her family in exchange for the help she gave the spies, just as the man from Luz was promised mercy.
Rahab and her family were spared when Jericho was captured, just as the man from Luz and his family were spared and allowed to leave in peace.
Abraham's servant asked God to show him mercy (חֶסֶד) by guiding him correctly, just as the guard asked the man to show them the entrance to the city.
David asked the king of Moab for protection for his parents and showed mercy in return—a similar pattern of mutual goodwill.
